question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), and \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\). Find the measure of \(\angle ADB\) in degrees.
solution: By SSS, \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD\), so \(\angle ADB=\angle ADC\). Also, \(\angle ADB+\angle ADC=180^\circ\), hence \(\angle ADB=90^\circ\).

reference.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), and \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\). Find the measure of \(\angle ADB\) in degrees.
reference.solution:
Method 1: SSS and equal supplementary angles

By SSS, \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD\), so \(\angle ADB=\angle ADC\). Also, \(\angle ADB+\angle ADC=180^\circ\), hence \(\angle ADB=90^\circ\).

Method 2: Use the isosceles median property

Since \(AB=AC\), the triangle is isosceles with base \(BC\). Because \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), \(AD\) is the median to the base. In an isosceles triangle, this median is also an altitude, so \(AD\perp BC\). Therefore \(\angle ADB=90^\circ\).
